recommendation: Use Claude Haiku 5.5 as the default. gpt-6-luna is fine as the staff fallback: cheaper per plan at list price, equal on the attack kit and intake accuracy; the cost is slower plans and more template wording.
recommendation_detail: Use Claude Haiku 5.5 as the default. Plan numbers are identical, the writing is about as good (a blind judge could not separate the two where both wrote AI text), safety is the same, and Haiku is twice as fast with far fewer template fallbacks (20% against 51%) and much better prompt caching.
gpt-6-luna is fine as the staff fallback: cheaper per plan at list price, equal on the attack kit and intake accuracy; the cost is slower plans and more template wording.
dollar_note: gpt-6-luna looks cheaper partly because 51% of its plans fell back to free templates. Counting only plans where the AI wrote the adviser text: $0.00187 against $0.00243 for Haiku.
caveats: Small samples: 80 plans, 40 pairs (28 real comparisons), 24 users, 57 messages. A gap of 2–3 wins is noise.
The judge (Sonnet) is a third model but from Anthropic, so it may lean to Claude's style; its "numbers right" calls are weak.
Both models ran at once on one machine; question and attack timeouts were a load effect.
The app's time caps (24 s a plan, 12 s a specialist) turn slow replies into templates; gpt-6-luna might do better with looser caps (not tested).
One run per condition; test mode.
